candidates.exact_span: The concentration in the sludge of each pollutant listed above in found in Element I, Section I, Table 1.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This recordkeeping obligation specifies which pollutant concentrations must be developed and retained on site. Interpreting which pollutants are 'listed above' in Element I Section I Table 1, or whether sludge recordkeeping applies to a given facility/discharge context, changes which monitoring evidence Purpose B treats as required and whether absent concentration records are documented no-data, inadequate evidence, or unresolved under Purpose C.

candidates.exact_span: The annual whole sludge application rate for the sewage sludge that does not cause the annual pollutant loading rates in Table 4 to be exceeded.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This ties sludge land-application compliance to Table 4 annual pollutant loading rates. Different readings of how the annual whole sludge application rate is calculated, which Table 4 pollutants/limits apply, or whether the no-exceedance condition is met would change enforceable numeric limit selection and exceedance evaluation under Purpose A and what supporting records Purpose B/C expect.

candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall report annually on the DMR the following information:
candidates.computation_change_reason: The annual DMR reporting cadence governs when sludge information must be submitted. Interpreting 'annually' against other passages requiring monthly-average pollutant concentrations (item 6.d) affects whether monitoring is required monthly, only at annual reporting, or on another schedule, changing Purpose B obligation timing and Purpose C classification of missing interim results.

candidates.exact_span: List Pollutant Table 4 appropriate for permittee's land application practices.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Permittee-specific selection of applicable Table 4 pollutants depends on interpreting 'appropriate for permittee's land application practices.' A different subset of Table 4 pollutants changes which annual pollutant loading limits are operative for Purpose A and which pollutants must be reported/monitored under Purpose B.

candidates.exact_span: The frequency of monitoring listed in Element 1, Section I.C. which applies to the permittee.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This cross-reference delegates the applicable monitoring frequency to Element 1 Section I.C. Resolving 'which applies to the permittee' and the referenced frequency table directly determines whether monitoring was required for each period under Purpose B.

TCLP is reported as Pass/Fail rather than a numeric concentration. Interpreting whether this is an enforceable numeric discharge limit, a separate compliance test, or report-only monitoring changes Purpose A limit-applicability analysis and how Purpose C treats absent or non-numeric TCLP results versus required monitoring gaps.

candidates.exact_span: The concentration (mg/Kg) in the sludge of each pollutant listed in Table 1 (defined as a monthly average) found in Element 1, Section I.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This passage defines reportable numeric pollutant concentrations in mg/Kg as monthly averages tied to Table 1 in Element 1 Section I. Interpretation of 'monthly average,' which Table 1 pollutants apply, and how reported values map to limits affects Purpose A exceedance comparisons, Purpose B monitoring/reporting requirements, and Purpose C handling of missing monthly sludge concentration data.

candidates.exact_span: Class A pathogen reduction Alternative used as listed in Section I.B.3.a. Alternatives describe how the pathogen reduction requirements are met.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The selected Class A pathogen reduction alternative is a permit condition that may determine which pathogen-related monitoring or reporting pathways apply. Different alternative selections or interpretations of the Section I.B.3.a list change Purpose B applicability and what documented evidence Purpose C expects when pathogen-related results are absent.

candidates.exact_span: Vector attraction reduction Alternative used as listed in Section I.B.4.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The vector attraction reduction alternative reported on the DMR may condition which vector-attraction monitoring or management evidence is required. Interpreting which Section I.B.4 alternative applies changes Purpose B monitoring obligations and Purpose C evaluation of missing related documentation.

candidates.exact_span: Annual sludge production in dry metric tons/year.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This is a distinct annual reporting parameter on the DMR. Whether sludge production reporting is required for a given permittee/period, and how 'annual' is measured, affects Purpose B monitoring-and-reporting obligation evaluation.

candidates.exact_span: Amount of sludge land applied in dry metric tons/year.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Land-applied sludge quantity is both a DMR reporting obligation and an input to Table 4 loading-rate compliance tied to item 5.e. Different interpretations of what counts as land-applied sludge or the reporting year boundary change Purpose A loading-rate calculations, Purpose B reporting requirements, and Purpose C treatment of missing quantity evidence.

candidates.exact_span: Amount of sludge transported interstate in dry metric tons/year.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interstate transport reporting may be required only when transport occurs. Interpreting whether transport happened, how interstate movement is identified, and whether zero or absent reporting satisfies the obligation affects Purpose B applicability and Purpose C classification of missing transport data.
